_comment: Accepted cross-platform attribute-effect findings, two kinds. DIVERGENCE ({fixture, platforms}): the control-diff verdict (active = the attribute changed the render, inert = it did not) disagrees across the platforms the attribute is declared for — semantic drift unless a deliberate platform idiom; the reason says which. UNIFORMLY-INERT ({fixture, verdict, declared}): a value the SSoT enumerates changes nothing on ANY platform — either it is the default rendering (say so in the reason) or it is dead/unimplemented everywhere. Unrecorded findings fail `jui conformance gate --cross-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and must be pruned (`jui conformance cross-effect --update`). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

adjudicated host-shim limitation (web), NOT a converter defect: the emitted class is `disabled:bg-<name>`, and the conformance host resolves palette names through a GENERATED plain-CSS shim (`.bg-dark_red { … }`) that carries no variants — so the base utility renders and the `disabled:` variant has nothing to resolve to. A consumer whose globals.css registers the colours in `@theme` gets the variant from Tailwind itself. Re-measure if the host stops needing the shim. Family: host-shim-variant-gap.
